info.title: Snajp CRM API
info.description:
Read and write the companies and people a Snajp customer keeps in Snajp CRM, and sync a customer
register in from another system.

**Authentication.** Send the key in `X-API-Key`. Keys are created under CRM, Developers, and carry
scopes: `crm:las` (read), `crm:skriv` (write), `crm:synk` (sync), `crm:admin` (connections).

**Idempotency.** Any POST accepts `Idempotency-Key`. Within 24 hours the same key and body return
the stored response, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

**Pagination.** Lists return `next_cursor`. Pass it as `cursor` until it is `null`.

**Rate limit.** 600 requests per minute and customer. `X-RateLimit-Remaining` is on every
response; a 429 carries `Retry-After`.

**Errors.** `{"detail": {"code", "message", "meddelande"}}`. `code` is stable, `message` is English,
`meddelande` is Swedish.

**Swedish formats.** Organisation numbers are checked with the Luhn digit and stored as
`NNNNNN-NNNN`. Phone numbers are stored as E.164, Swedish postal codes as `NNN NN`, dates as ISO 8601.

**Keeping a copy in sync.** Read `GET /changes` from your last `next_cursor`: one feed for every
object, in order. Or have Snajp call you: register a webhook under `/webhooks`. Listing with
`sort=updated&include_deleted=true&updated_since=<your last sync>` works as before. Deleted
records carry `deleted_at` and must be removed on your side as well.

**Webhooks.** Each delivery is a POST with `X-Snajp-Signature: t=<unix time>,v1=<hex>`, where `v1`
is HMAC-SHA256 over `"{t}.{body}"` with the webhook's secret. Answer 2xx within ten seconds.
Anything else is retried seven times over about a day. Events for people, sole proprietors and
private persons are thin: `id`, `object`, `type`, `occurred_at` and the changed `fields`, never the
record. Fetch it with your key.

**Suppressions.** One block for every channel: `/suppressions` holds emails, domains, phone numbers
and organisation numbers that must not be contacted, with channel, reason and date.
`POST /suppressions/check` answers whether anything in Snajp blocks a contact.

**SCB's business register.** `GET /lookup/companies?org_number=` looks a company up without saving,
and `POST /companies/{id}/enrich` fills its empty fields. Company level only, never people, and a
sole proprietorship is not looked up.

get.summary: Everything that has happened with a company, newest first
get.description:
The record's own changes, the work linked to it here (notes,
activities, tasks and deals), together with what has happened elsewhere
in Snajp: Iris leads for the same organisation number (emails sent,
replies, calls, status changes, notes, tasks) and support tickets from
the company's people. Composed when read; nothing is copied. `origin`
says where an entry lives: `crm`, `iris` or `support`.

Drafts that were never sent are not history and are left out. Support
tickets carry subject, channel and status, never the messages. A key
with scopes gets no excerpts (`text` is null): it learns that
something happened and where, not what was written.

get.summary: The company's leads in Iris and what they mean here
get.description:
`do_not_contact` is true when the record says so OR when one of the
company's leads has asked not to be contacted: that outcome always
wins over a value here that would reopen the lead.

schema.title: Response Iris Bolag Api Crm V1 Companies  Company Id  Iris Get

post.summary: Set an outcome on a company and on its leads
post.description:
The outcome is carried out in the leads flow as well, by the same
functions a call from the call list uses: pending sends are stopped,
the lead changes status, and `do_not_contact` blocks the address.
`won` makes the company a customer. A company without a lead only
gets the change on the record itself.

post.summary: Block an email, domain, phone number or organisation number
post.description:
201 with the new suppression, or 200 with the one that already blocks
the same value in the same channel. Sends `suppression.created`.

post.summary: Add many suppressions in one call, e.g. your NIX check
post.description:
Upload the outcome of your own NIX check with `channel: phone,
reason: nix`. `added + already_blocked + len(invalid)` is the number of
values sent; a duplicate within the call counts as already blocked.
`invalid` gives the position and the reason, never the value.

delete.description:
The suppression stays as a record with `lifted_at`, and no longer
blocks. Lifting it again changes nothing. Sends `suppression.lifted`.

post.summary: Is a contact blocked anywhere in Snajp?
post.description:
Reads every source together: the suppression list (including domain
and `all` blocks), records marked do-not-contact (every private person
is), unsubscribed addresses (email only) and leads that asked not to be
contacted. `sources` says which ones blocked: `suppression_list`,
`record`, `unsubscribed`, `lead`. Nothing about the contact is returned.

schema.title: Response Kontrollera Api Crm V1 Suppressions Check Post

get.summary: Look up a company in SCB's business register, without saving
get.description:
Company level only: name, legal form, status, SNI codes, registered
office, postal address, employee size class and advertising block.
Never people: no signatories, no board, no owner names. A sole
proprietorship is not looked up (422 `not_a_company`): its number is
the owner's personal identity number. Nothing is stored.

schema.title: Response Sla Upp Bolag Api Crm V1 Lookup Companies Get

post.summary: Fill a company's empty fields from SCB's business register
post.description:
Fills `name`, `legal_form`, `sni_code` and the address where they are
empty, and always sets `registry_status`. `filled` and `skipped` name
the fields: skipped are fields where the register differs but the
company's own value was kept. The employee size class is returned under
`registry` but not written to `employees`, which is a count.

An advertising block in the register is returned as
`advertising_block` and does NOT mark the company do-not-contact. Add
a suppression under `/suppressions` if you want it to block.

parameters.name: overwrite

schema.description: Also replace fields that have a value, except fields someone changed by hand in Snajp.
schema.title: Overwrite

parameters.description: Also replace fields that have a value, except fields someone changed by hand in Snajp.

postal_code.title: Postal Code
postal_code.description: Postal code. Swedish codes are stored as `NNN NN`.

channel.title: Channel
channel.description: `all` asks whether anything blocks in any channel.

org_number.title: Org Number
org_number.description: Swedish organisationsnummer. `556036-0793`, `5560360793`, `16556036-0793` and `SE556036079301` are all accepted. The check digit is verified. Unique per customer: posting an existing number updates that company.

relation.title: Relation
relation.description: Defaults to `customer`. `not_relevant` is a company that has said no or does not fit: unlike `former_customer` it stays excluded from Iris runs and lists.

private_person.title: Private Person
private_person.description: The customer is a private person, not a company. No personal identity number is stored, and the record is always `do_not_contact`: it is left out of every send, list and Iris run.

custom.title: Custom
custom.description: Your own fields, up to 50 scalar values.

name.title: Name
name.description: Your name for the source, e.g. `hubspot`. Unique.

mapping.title: Mapping
mapping.description: Overrides on top of the system's default mapping, per object and target field. See GET /connections/systems for the defaults and the format.

missing_records.title: Missing Records
missing_records.description: What a completed full sync does with records the source no longer has.

include_private_persons.title: Include Private Persons
include_private_persons.description: Off by default: records the source marks as private persons are skipped (`reason: privatperson`). Turn it on to store them, marked `private_person` and `do_not_contact`.

stage_id.title: Stage Id
stage_id.description: Defaults to the first open stage. Changing it puts the deal last in the new stage; use POST /deals/{id}/move to place it.

probability.title: Probability
probability.description: Own win probability. `null` uses the stage's.

lost_reason.title: Lost Reason
lost_reason.description: Free text, at most 500 characters. The fallback beside `lost_reason_code`, and may be set with any code.

lost_reason_code.title: Lost Reason Code
lost_reason_code.description: Why the deal was lost, from a fixed list: `price`, `competitor`, `timing`, `no_need`, `no_budget`, `no_response` or `other`. Any other value is refused with `invalid_fields` (code `forlustorsak_okand`). `null` clears it.

custom.title: Custom
custom.description: Your own fields, up to 50 scalar values.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: Without it: a value with @ is an email, otherwise a domain on `email` and a phone number on `phone` and `all`.

stage_id.title: Stage Id
stage_id.description: The stage to move the deal to. May be its current stage.

before_id.title: Before Id
before_id.description: Place the deal just before this deal in the stage.

after_id.title: After Id
after_id.description: Place the deal just after this deal. Without either, last.

email.title: Email
email.description: Unique per customer: posting an existing address updates that person.

company_id.title: Company Id
company_id.description: Id of a company in Snajp CRM.

legal_basis.title: Legal Basis
legal_basis.description: GDPR article 6 basis for holding the person.

source_type.title: Source Type
source_type.description: Where the information about the person first came from (GDPR article 14): `company_website`, `registry`, `customer_provided` (the customer gave it), `sync`, `manual` or `other`. Any other value is refused with `invalid_fields` (code `kalltyp_okand`). Optional: leave it out when it is not known. Not the same as `source`, which says how the record came into Snajp.

source_name.title: Source Name
source_name.description: The source by name, e.g. the web address or the register. At most 300 characters.

collected_at.title: Collected At
collected_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp the information was collected. Defaults to when the person is created.

mapping.title: Mapping
mapping.description: Try a mapping without saving it.

ids.title: Ids
ids.description: Every stage id, each once, in the new order.

name.title: Name
name.description: Unique per workspace, at most 60 characters. Required when creating.

color.title: Color
color.description: A colour token name, free text.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: What `value` is. An email or domain block belongs to `email` or `all`, a phone block to `phone` or `all`; an organisation number blocks the company in any channel.

value.title: Value
value.description: Stored normalised: email and domain in lower case, phone as E.164, organisation number as NNNNNN-NNNN.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: `objection` is GDPR art. 21, `nix` a hit in your NIX check.

note.title: Note
note.description: Never sent in a webhook or written to a log.

status.title: Status
status.description: Defaults to `todo`. `completed_at` is set when it becomes `done`.

url.title: Url
url.description: A public https address. Required when creating.

events.title: Events
events.description: Event types to receive, e.g. `company.updated`. `*` (the default) is all of them. GET /webhooks/events lists them.

active.title: Active
active.description: Turning a disabled webhook on again resets its failure count.
